paretoBreakdown.explanation: Both V2 and the second-pass reviewer now share the identical 9-state vocabulary (this phase's core fix), yet still disagree on which of {REVIEW_REQUIRED_FLAG_ONLY, HONESTLY_UNRESOLVED, DISCOVERY_ONLY_NOT_REPRESENTED, UNSUPPORTED_SILENT} best describes a given case. In the dominant pattern (V2 says REVIEW_REQUIRED_FLAG_ONLY or HONESTLY_UNRESOLVED; the reviewer says UNSUPPORTED_SILENT), V2's own matching.ts logic credits a 'flag' or 'unresolved' status to a candidate that only weakly or tangentially relates to the claim - the second-pass reviewer, applying the protocol's own instruction to treat weak/tangential text with real skepticism, judges that nothing in the packet plausibly relates to the claim at all, so no flag or unresolved-signal 'counts.' This is a genuine, newly-visible calibration gap in V2's own threshold for what counts as a corresponding-enough candidate to earn a safety-flag credit - previously invisible because the old second-pass protocol's coarse vocabulary collapsed all of these into one 'UNREPRESENTED' bucket, masking the disagreement entirely (see 01-original-disagreement-forensics.json's STATE_TAXONOMY_MISMATCH finding). Fixing the vocabulary mismatch surfaced this different, previously-hidden problem rather than eliminating disagreement.

A newly-observed, distinct disagreement type not present in the original forensics: V2 detected an active material conflict (CONTRADICTORY matchStatus - a candidate actively asserts something incompatible with the claim), while the second-pass reviewer, reading the same candidates, judged them simply irrelevant (UNSUPPORTED_SILENT) rather than contradictory. This suggests V2's conflict-detection layer (conflicts.ts) may be flagging a conflict on candidates a careful human reader would not consider related enough to conflict with the claim in the first place - a distinct question from the safe-surfacing threshold issue above, since CONTRADICTORY is arguably a MORE severe disposition than a plain non-match, not merely a different flavor of no-credit.

headlineConclusion: None of the 6 genuine credit disagreements are new; both are carried-forward, already-documented V2 defects/unresolved questions from the original forensics, unchanged by this phase (as expected, since no V2 logic was touched). The dominant story in this rerun is the 31-case SAFE_SURFACING_TAXONOMY_THRESHOLD_DISAGREEMENT cluster: giving the second-pass reviewer V2's own vocabulary successfully eliminated the PREVIOUS masking artifact (65.6% of the original disagreements) but revealed a real, substantive, and previously invisible disagreement about V2's own threshold for crediting a 'flag' or 'unresolved' signal to a weakly-related candidate. This is a genuine, actionable finding for a future V2 iteration: tighten the correspondence bar required before a candidate's own gap-flag or self-declared-uncertainty is allowed to count toward REVIEW_REQUIRED_FLAG_ONLY / HONESTLY_UNRESOLVED, rather than the current apparent behavior of crediting these states too liberally on tangentially-related candidates.
